MachineSetup, which StartLevelLoad reaches through the vector at $3FF6 when the engine's own load (or Central Park's title load) put JMP $0E00 there; the later levels' title loads point that vector at an RTS. Only the first run finds this code: every level load keeps pages 0 to 3 at $0C00-$0FFF (see $0F00). With interrupts off it maps RAM with the I/O ($00 = $2F, $01 = $35), turns off the CIA interrupts and the raster interrupt, stops CIA 1's two timers ($DC0E and $DC0F), clears the sprite expansion and priority registers, silences the SID ($D418), sets the CIA port directions, zeroes the sprite positions, clears $0200-$02FF, the sprite buffers $0C00-$0DFF and the zero page from $02 to $FF. It then tells PAL from NTSC: it asks for a raster interrupt at line 304 ($D012 = $30 with bit 7 of $D011 set), waits for the raster to pass through lines 256 and up once, and keeps the interrupt flag in $AB: 1 when line 304 came (PAL, 312 lines), 0 when it did not (NTSC, 263). The interrupt routine plays the tune on only five ticks in six while $AB is zero ($1F0A), so the music keeps its PAL speed at 60 Hz. Then it points the NMI vectors ($0318 and $FFFA) at the RTI at $1582, sets up the state the first level starts from (below) and the bitmap screen ($140B).

Open the selected packed level file and backward-expand its title and playable occupants. Inputs: three-byte filename at `$117D` (`0n*`, n the level's digit), device 8, packed stream from the current disk side. Outputs: title occupant first, then, after Space or fire on either joystick port, the playable occupant; returns at end of file. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, `$02`, `$F6-$FF`, coding-table tail `$17F3-$17F5`, file/channel state. Hardware: replaces IRQ vector low byte temporarily, switches `$01` among all-RAM and KERNAL/I/O-visible states, polls CIA 1 fire, silences SID, and uses VIC border writes as read activity indication. Actual bytes are written from `upper` down through `lower+1`.

Store the first already-read byte of a packed level header, read the remainder of the eight-byte loader header, and continue the resident backward decompression path.
Inputs: A is the first header byte and X=0. The KERNAL-backed byte reader at $EE13 is available; the current level file/channel is open; loader pass counter $02 and packed-stream state are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $FB, reads four further bytes into $FC-$FF (upper output cursor $FC/$FD and lower bound $FE/$FF), then reads exactly three more bytes through STA $17EE,X for X=5,6,7, filling the header-supplied distance-width slots $17F3-$17F5. The complete header is eight bytes. It then clears $F6-$FA and expands the selected occupant. On the pass boundary it re-enters this same header tail at $1029 for the next segment.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02, $F6-$FF, $17F3-$17F5, destination memory, loader stack frames, and KERNAL file/channel state along the continued load path.
Hardware: The continued loader switches CPU-port $01 between all-RAM and KERNAL/I/O-visible mappings, uses KERNAL serial input, polls CIA 1 at $DC00/$DC01 on the pass boundary, silences SID at $D418, and writes VIC-II border $D020 while it reads literal bytes (not during the header reads or the bit-reservoir refills).

Return the next packed-stream bit, refill the sentinel-marked one-byte reservoir when it empties, and perform the exact inter-segment or final-load transition when the output cursor reaches its boundary. Inputs: Bit reservoir $FB; destination cursor $FC/$FD; segment boundary $FE/$FF; remaining-segment state $02; KERNAL serial-input status $90; and an active packed input channel. Outputs: On an ordinary path carry is the next decoded bit and $FB holds the shifted or renewed reservoir. Boundary paths close or advance the input, return to the loaded phase, or display the preceding title and wait before decoding the next segment. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, $01, $02, $90, $FB, and transition scratch on boundary paths. Hardware: Temporarily changes CPU-port banking; boundary paths may clear and close the KERNAL channel, enable interrupts, poll CIA 1, tick music, silence SID volume, and invoke the phase title renderer.

Select literal-input mode by writing SEC at the shared copy-mode instruction, then fall through to the backward token-copy loop so every output byte comes from KERNAL serial input. Inputs: Run/page state $F7/$F8; destination cursor $FC/$FD; page companion $FA; an active KERNAL input channel; and writable code at $1151. Outputs: Literal bytes are read through $EE13 and stored backward through ($FC),Y; $F8/$FA and $FC/$FD advance to the next decode position while $F7 is preserved. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $F8, $FA, $FC/$FD, $01, self-modified byte $1151, and border color $D020; X, $F7, and $F9 are preserved. Hardware: Each serial read exposes KERNAL ROM, then sets $01 to $30 (all RAM, like the $00 the decoder stores at $104A), and increments then normalizes VIC-II border color $D020 as a load indicator.

Execute the shared backward token-copy loop, taking bytes from the LZ match pointer in CLC mode or from KERNAL serial input in SEC mode. Inputs: Run/page state $F7/$F8; match pointer $F9/$FA; destination cursor $FC/$FD; and mode opcode CLC $18 or SEC $38 self-installed at $1151. Outputs: Decoded bytes are stored backward through ($FC),Y; $F8/$FA and $FC/$FD advance to the next token position while $F7 and $F9 are preserved. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $F8, $FA, and $FC/$FD; literal mode also changes $01 and $D020. X and $F7/$F9 are preserved. Hardware: Match mode has no I/O effect. Literal mode exposes KERNAL ROM, reads through $EE13, sets $01 to $30 (all RAM) afterwards, and updates VIC-II border color $D020.

The six clock digits' offsets from $1C77: 0 and 1 (hours), 10 and 11 (minutes), 20 and 21 (seconds), one in each of the three text records that draw the clock. The clock's tick ($1F2C), SaveLevelState ($1C58) and the level's start use them, and The Basement and The Office copy the minutes and seconds (offsets 10 to 21) into the lock code at $0297.

Where each clock digit turns over, as glyph numbers ($1B is 0): $25 for the hours' two digits, the minutes' second and the seconds' second (after 9), and $21 for the minutes' first and the seconds' first (after 5). The clock's tick adds one second every 50 passes ($0228), working from the last digit and carrying while a digit reaches its limit, which sets it back to $1B; then it asks for a redraw ($022F).

The enemy's energy spiral: for each of the 44 half-cells of energy, the offset from $06FA of the screen cell it lies in. The cells run round a square spiral in columns 2 to 6 of rows 19 to 23 (offsets 161 and 160, then up and round to the centre). The first 22 are filled, half a cell at a time, with $09 (brown in the low nibble), the next 22 a second time with $89 (orange in the high nibble as well); an empty cell is $00. The interrupt routine moves the shown energy $022C one step toward the real one $022A every second pass and recolours the cell ($1E7B, $1E9C).

The player's energy spiral, laid out as the enemy's in columns 8 to 12 of rows 19 to 23, the mirror image: offsets from $06FA, 44 of them, the first 22 coloured $02 (red) and the second 22 $A2 (light red as well). The interrupt routine moves the shown energy $022B toward the player's energy $0229 and recolours the cell ($1E82, $1EA3).
